text: Every plane in America got stuck on the ground, and it all started with one little box in Arkansas.
On Friday, a brand new router, the kind of box that moves internet traffic, started flooding the air traffic network.
It fired about a thousand calls every five seconds, and the old computers running the radar fell way behind.
Seventeen air traffic centers went shaky, every plane was held on the ground, and over twelve thousand flights got canceled.
Then on Monday, a software bug blocked people from their bank accounts at Chase and other big banks.
Today, the top secret computer network at the NSA went down during routine fixes.
And Apple pushed one inside update that broke iCloud sign in for every single user.
Everyone wanted to know if America was being hacked. Officials said no.
Here's the scary part. Big systems are so connected that one mistake can spread to millions of machines at once.
In 2024, one bad update from a company called CrowdStrike crashed about eight and a half million computers.
Planes, hospitals and banks all froze. No hacker at all. Just one bad file.
Follow for more of the hidden stuff behind the news.
